boards.title: Your First Weekend at Gettysburg College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning campus landmarks, finding student spaces, and connecting Gettysburg College with the surrounding history.

cards.title: Start at the College’s Historic Center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Pennsylvania Hall
cards.notes: Meet outside Penn Hall, identify its cupola and porticoes, and use this central landmark to orient yourself before exploring campus.
cards.short_summary: Begin with the original campus building and a dependable visual reference point.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College states that Pennsylvania Hall was built in 1837, was the original College building, and remains a focal point for Convocation and Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an exterior orientation stop; the building currently contains administrative offices.

cards.title: Learn Your Main Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Friday dinner · Servo
cards.notes: Use dinner to learn the serving areas, locate dietary selections, and practice entering with the student ID tied to your meal plan.
cards.short_summary: Get comfortable navigating the campus dining hall used by first-year meal plans.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College identifies the Dining Center as “Servo,” says it serves food seven days a week, and requires first-year students to maintain the Unlimited Servo Entry plan.
cards.access_notes: Operating hours vary; consult Dining Services before going. Entry uses a meal plan or another accepted payment method.

cards.title: Find the Campus Information Hub
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · College Union Building
cards.notes: Locate the information desk, scan the event displays, and try a lobby game while learning where student-service offices are housed.
cards.short_summary: Use the student union as a practical base for directions, services, and casual recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says the CUB contains dining and student services; its lobby has board games, arcade games, video-game systems, a television, and a pool table.
cards.access_notes: The desk is staffed until 11 p.m. during semesters; students can enter the CUB 24/7 with their College ID.

cards.title: Set Up Your Library Routine
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Musselman Library
cards.notes: Find the main service desk, charging lockers, and lower-level study room so you know where to return when coursework begins.
cards.short_summary: Map essential study and research services before the first busy academic week.
cards.evidence_claim: Musselman Library provides research assistance and offers a lower-level reservable study room plus charging lockers on its main level.
cards.access_notes: Room reservations are limited to College community members; building access after 8 p.m. requires a current College ID.

cards.title: Add an Art Break
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · Schmucker Hall
cards.notes: Walk through the current exhibitions, note the gallery’s main-floor location, and check its calendar for future talks and programs.
cards.short_summary: Pair a campus walk with a changing exhibition in a publicly accessible gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: Schmucker Art Gallery is located on the main floor of Schmucker Hall and is free and open to the public Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; verify exhibition dates before visiting because installations change.

cards.entity_name: John F. Jaeger Center for Athletics, Recreation and Fitness
cards.title: Tour the Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Jaeger Center
cards.notes: Bring your student ID, locate the fitness and climbing areas, and review posted schedules before planning a first workout or swim.
cards.short_summary: Learn the layout of the College’s central recreation and fitness facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College describes the Jaeger Center as containing a fitness center, bouldering area, 30-foot climbing tower, fitness-class room, gym and natatorium.
cards.access_notes: Student IDs are required for Jaeger Center access; consult the current Campus Recreation schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Pause Beside Quarry Pond
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon · West Campus
cards.notes: Walk to the pavilion in daylight, use its picnic tables for a group check-in, and note the nearby athletic fields for later events.
cards.short_summary: Take an outdoor pause at a named campus gathering place overlooking the pond.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College says Quarry Pavilion overlooks Quarry Pond, sits near athletic fields, and is equipped with picnic tables and charcoal grills.
cards.access_notes: Use during daylight and observe any posted reservation or event restrictions; grill use requires appropriate planning and supervision.

cards.title: See What Is Playing Downtown
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · 25 Carlisle Street
cards.notes: Check the official calendar, choose an age-appropriate film or performance, and buy through the theater’s site or box office only.
cards.short_summary: Connect campus with downtown through the College-owned historic theater.
cards.evidence_claim: The Majestic Theater says Gettysburg College purchased it in 1988; its official ticket page lists cinema and live-event sales at 25 Carlisle Street.
cards.access_notes: Box-office hours are Monday–Friday 3–7:30 p.m., Saturday noon–7:30 p.m., and Sunday 1–5:30 p.m.; event times vary.

cards.entity_name: Gettysburg National Military Park Museum and Visitor Center
cards.title: Begin the Battlefield Visit Indoors
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Gettysburg National Military Park
cards.notes: Start at the visitor center for orientation, ask what can be seen within your available time, and follow all bag-inspection rules.
cards.short_summary: Get official context and practical guidance before exploring the battlefield landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the Museum and Visitor Center as the place to begin a battlefield visit and lists daily seasonal operating hours.
cards.source_title: Operating Hours & Seasons - Gettysburg National Military Park
cards.access_notes: Open daily 8 a.m.–5 p.m. March–November and 9 a.m.–4 p.m. December–February; bags are subject to inspection.

cards.title: Understand the First-Year Walk Route
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Christ Chapel to the National Cemetery
cards.notes: Trace the documented route in daylight with friends, noting how campus connects to town and the National Cemetery before Orientation.
cards.short_summary: Close the weekend by learning the path of a documented Gettysburg College tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College documents an annual First-Year Walk that begins at Christ Chapel, proceeds through town, and concludes at Gettysburg National Military Park.
cards.source_title: 3 things to know about Orientation for the Class of 2027
cards.access_notes: The official group walk occurs during Orientation; this card suggests learning the public route in daylight, not staging the ceremony independently.
